name: Atlas
author: brodgar
description: Example addon (037-map-database): A LIVE MINIMAP PANEL BUILT FROM THE MAP DATABASE ALONE. The corner minimap is the client drawing the map file; this is the same picture from the other side — nothing here reads the live world except the one question 'where am I' (hafen.world.gridPos(), the anchor {gridId, x, y} that is the only thing the two halves share), and everything it SHOWS comes out of hafen.map: hafen.map.grid(gridId) is the door into the database, grid:image(lvl) is the recorded ground as an ordinary IMAGE HANDLE, and grid:segment():markers() are the pins recorded on that same explored area. THE PANEL COSTS NOTHING TO PAINT, and that is the claim this addon exists to make: an image handle goes into the stylesheet as bg = {image = …}, so the ENGINE paints the map every frame and this addon runs ZERO draw callbacks and ZERO widget callbacks while a live map is on screen — its whole cost is a four-per-second timer asking 'did the picture change?', and a timer is charged to `timers`, never to `draw` (read it in hafen.client:profiling():addons(), or run the 037.5 suite, which asserts exactly that on this addon's row). ':atlas pins' is the other half of that measurement rather than a decoration: the markers are drawn from Lua, so the panel is rebuilt WITH an onDraw and the same row starts reading one draw callback per frame — a zero only means something beside a number that is not zero. The LOAD MODEL is the caller's side of D-095: grid:image answers nil while it renders and the same handle once it has, so the timer is both the retry loop and the change test, and there is no callback to register and no ready event to wait for. A LEVEL IS A SCALE, NOT A SIZE: every drawing is 100x100 pixels, so ':atlas zoom 2' does not grow the panel, it makes each pixel sixteen tiles and the same square shows 4x4 grids of explored ground — which is also why the panel re-skins only when the player crosses into a new picture. Commands: ':atlas' opens/closes the panel; 'zoom <0..8>'; 'pins' toggles the Lua marker layer; 'where' prints the player's anchor beside the segment id and grid coord this client invented (look at those, never store them); 'mark [name]' drops a player marker at your feet — the one ungated write on this page, client-local and reversible by hand. SAFE-tier: declares no permissions and sends nothing to the server.
